thread:
sasha: heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix/KV cache hit-rate for prod us-west-2 starting ~03:30 UTC. Grafana shows ~40% -> ~5% on the prefix-cache panel :eyes:

alex: ugh. can you paste the dashboard panel link and a prom query? want to see if it's total requests spiking or misses rising.

sasha: panel: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/XYz12ab/prefix-cache-overview?orgId=1 (top card 'prefix hit rate by prefix_type')
prom query I used:```
sum by(prefix_type) (rate(kv_prefix_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(prefix_type) (rate(kv_prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```

maria: deploy-bot shows a canary push at 03:11 -> 03:12 (canary v13 rolled, then rolled back at 03:16). might be related: https://deploys.internal.redwood/runs/2026-03-17-0311

jon: pulling logs now. which service do you want me to grep? kv-proxy or kv-reader?

sasha: start with kv-proxy (it surfaces prefix misses). check for increased 5xx or routing errors. also check `kv_prefix_evictions_total` and `kv_prefix_cache_size_bytes`.

jon: on it. quick commands:
```bash
# prom query via curl (api)
curl -s "https://prom.internal.redwood/api/v1/query?query=sum%20(rate(kv_prefix_cache_requests_total%5B5m%5D))%20by(prefix_type)" | jq .
# look for evictions
curl -s "https://prom.internal.redwood/api/v1/query?query=rate(kv_prefix_evictions_total%5B5m%5D)" | jq .
```

infra-bot: notice: alert "kv-prefix-hitrate-low" fired in prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T03:35:12Z (fired for 6m). Alert rule: hitrate < 0.2 for 5m.

alex: if the evictions spike matches the hit-rate drop that points to memory pressure or a config change. can someone check instance memory and pod restarts? `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=kv-proxy -o wide`

maria: checking nodes now. no OOMs, but I see a config flag changed in canary: `prefix_cache.max_entries` was lowered from 2_000_000 -> 200_000 in the canary config. that would explain the drop for affected traffic.

sasha: thanks — so it's a rollout issue. action items: 1) silence the noisy alert (it's firing correctly but we don't need pager flood) 2) revert canary or roll forward with correct config 3) create follow-up to add a pre-deploy canary check for cache config mismatches.

maria: I'll open the revert PR and a terraform alert tweak. I'll also silence the alert for 30m: https://alerts.internal.redwood/alerts/kv-prefix-hitrate-low

alex: for the alert tuning proposal: current rule uses absolute threshold 0.2 which is fine for prod, but we should add a suppression window tied to deploys and an auto-mute when we detect config rollouts. Example alert tweak (Grafana alert rule snippet):```json
{
  "conditions": [{"type":"lt","threshold":0.2}],
  "mute_during_deploy": true,
  "snooze_for": "30m"
}
```

jon: logs show a sharp jump in `cache_miss_count` starting 03:13 from hosts that were in the canary cohort. grouping by `instance` matches the rollout. attaching a short trace link: https://jaeger.internal.redwood/trace/abcd-1234. trace shows increased backend calls for prefix resolution.

sasha: perfect. maria — please link the PRs here when ready. once reverted we'll re-evaluate metrics and re-enable the alert. also adding a tiny runbook note: if you see hit-rate < 0.1 and evictions spike -> check recent config changes, check canary tags, and rollback if config looks wrong.

maria: PRs: revert kv-proxy config: https://git.internal.redwood/r/infra/kv-proxy/pull/482 and alert tweak: https://git.internal.redwood/r/infra/alerts/pull/197. silenced alert for 30m.

sasha: awesome — thanks everyone. marking this thread resolved after we confirm metrics back to normal. :white_check_mark:

jon: metrics back to ~42% after rollback and canary drained (03:52). leaving a note in the incident board.

sasha: closing here, will add the runbook entry.
